Verified: every readable bookmark shows a **"Saved copy"** you can open, PDFs show **"Saved PDF,"** and the Internet Archive copy can be added on demand.

Reload **http://maker:4001**.

**New feature — preserving a saved copy.** Walk through it:

1. Each bookmark now shows a green-dotted **"Saved copy · date"** (and the aqueduct one shows **"Saved PDF"**). Click **"Saved copy"** on the MDN bookmark — a new tab opens the **preserved page as it was when you bookmarked it**, with a banner showing the capture date and original address. Click **"Saved PDF"** on the aqueduct paper — it indicates the **actual PDF file was kept**.
2. A **private copy is always kept automatically** for every readable page. The **Internet Archive** copy is **optional**: on a card without one, click **"Send to Internet Archive"** — it adds an **"Internet Archive copy"** link. The Rome article already has one.
3. Save a new link (e.g. `https://reactjs.org/docs/hooks-intro.html`). On the save form you'll see the note that a copy is always kept, plus an optional **"Also save a copy to the Internet Archive"** checkbox. Save and see the "Saved copy" appear on the new card.
4. For the **unreadable** case (`https://blocked.example/secret-report`), it still shows **"No saved copy yet"**, and the retry (when the page becomes reachable) now also **captures the copy**.

A few things to confirm, and one honesty note:
- **Local copy automatic, Internet Archive optional** — right split?
- Preserving the **actual PDF file** for PDFs (vs. just a rendered page) — correct expectation?
- Should the saved copy be **captured once at save time** and left as-is, or would you ever want to **refresh/re-capture** it later (e.g. the page meaningfully changed)?

> Honesty note: this prototype runs **offline**, so the saved copy and the Internet Archive submission are **simulated stand-ins** to show the behavior and where it appears — no real page or archive.org call happens here. The real capture would happen in the built app.

How does preservation feel?
